cur:catacombs-arles-samaritan.summary: In the left panel of this strigilated front, Christ speaks with the Samaritan woman at the well, whose wheel and rope are carved beside her; below is a further scene with Christ. The quiet conversation at the well recalls the promise of the 'living water' of eternal life.
facts: The museum calls it 'part of a strigilated sarcophagus called the Samaritan Woman'.
Scenes were often placed only in the end panels of strigilated sarcophagi, leaving the centre to the wavy strigils.

cur:objects-berlin-trier-christ-enthrone.summary: Christ sits enthroned in a mandorla at the centre of the plaque, raising his hand in blessing, beneath a draped curtain. Around him the four evangelists sit writing at their desks, each inspired by his symbol, so that the Gospels seem to flow from the Lord in majesty. The composition presents Christ as the living Word proclaimed by the four Gospels.
facts: According to the photographer's documentation the plaque was donated to the Berlin museum by J. Werner in 1898 (inv. 2423).
Christ in Majesty surrounded by the evangelists was a favourite subject for the front covers of Ottonian gospel books (type).

walters:71.273.summary: Two ivory leaves, divided by slender colonnettes beneath crocketed arches, tell the story of Christ in eight scenes. The lower register shows the Annunciation, the Nativity, the Adoration of the Magi and the Entry into Jerusalem; the upper shows the Last Supper, the Agony in the Garden, the Crucifixion and the Entombment. Reading from bottom to top, the owner could follow Christ from his conception to the tomb.
walters:71.273.scripture: Luke 1:26–38; Luke 2:1–20; Matthew 2:1–12; Matthew 21:1–11; Matthew 26:20–46; John 19:16–42
facts: The Walters attributes it to the 'Atelier of the Diptychs with Colonnettes', a group of ivories consistent in style, with doll-like figures and exaggerated gestures.
Its silver hinges are set diagonally.
It passed through the Becker (1898) and Thomé (1906) sales in Cologne and the dealer Jacques Seligmann before Henry Walters bought it in 1912.
walters:71.273.notes: Worklist year 800 was a parsing error for '3rd quarter 14th century'.
